drills.q: Given V=100,000 nodes and E=150,000 edges, which representation should you use and why?
drills.a: Adjacency list -- the graph is sparse (E close to V). An adjacency matrix would need V^2 = 10^10 cells, infeasible in memory.

drills.q: Implement cycle detection for an undirected graph. What's the critical detail that's easy to forget?
drills.a: DFS tracking the parent node; a visited neighbor is only a real cycle if it's NOT the parent you just came from -- forgetting parent exclusion makes every single edge look like a cycle.

drills.q: Course Schedule: given prerequisite pairs, determine if all courses can be completed. Why can't you use the same visited-check as undirected cycle detection?
drills.a: Directed graphs need three-color state (white/gray/black): an edge to a fully-processed (black) node can be a valid DAG convergence, not a cycle. Only an edge to a GRAY (currently active ancestor) node is a real cycle -- binary visited/unvisited can't distinguish these two cases.

drills.q: Design a bipartite check for 'Possible Bipartition' (split people into two groups given dislike pairs) and state the exact mathematical condition being tested.
drills.a: BFS/DFS 2-coloring: assign opposite colors to adjacent nodes; a conflict means not bipartite. The exact condition: a graph is bipartite if and only if it has no odd-length cycle -- the coloring attempt is a complete decision procedure for this.

drills.q: Design a multi-source BFS for 'rotten oranges spread to fresh neighbors each minute.' Why is this faster than running BFS once per source?
drills.a: Initialize the queue with all rotten-orange sources simultaneously at distance 0, then run standard BFS once -- O(V+E) total, versus O(k*(V+E)) if you ran BFS separately from each of k sources and took the minimum.

drills.q: Design a system that incrementally rejects any new dependency edge that would create a directed cycle in a build/dependency graph, added one edge at a time. Why doesn't plain Union-Find solve this?
drills.a: Union-Find only tracks undirected connectivity -- two nodes being in the same component doesn't tell you if a directed path exists in a specific direction, which is what matters for a circular dependency (A depends on B depends on A). You need an incrementally-maintained topological order (e.g., online topological sort) or a bounded local DFS from the new edge's target checking reachability to its source.
